RagShortTexts: Prussian leaders had different kin ties and views on Order demands.
Musters required food and home defense agreements, not merely shared enemies.

Variants.Content: Prussian leaders had ties to kin, settlements and neighboring posts and could differ over Order levies and missions. Mustering required agreement over food, home defense and passage; a distant letter alone might not bring scattered communities into action.

Prussian leaders had ties to kin, settlements and neighboring posts and could differ over Order levies and missions. Mustering required agreement over food, home defense and passage; a distant letter alone might not bring scattered communities into action. Fighters needed food and animals, moving differently with booty on return. Coordinated movement depended on messages, relationships and accepted risks.

Prussian leaders had ties to kin, settlements and neighboring posts and could differ over Order levies and missions. Mustering required agreement over food, home defense and passage; a distant letter alone might not bring scattered communities into action. Leaders sought people through purposes, shares and defense arrangements. Heavy kin losses weakened later musters, and failed distributions damaged authority.

Prussian leaders had ties to kin, settlements and neighboring posts and could differ over Order levies and missions. Mustering required agreement over food, home defense and passage; a distant letter alone might not bring scattered communities into action. A household supplying fighters lost labor for fields, animals and repairs. Booty could help, but delay, wounds and animal losses burdened kin and made shared work important.
